# The Dark Elves

*Pages PDF 4-8*

## ## **the Dark Elves**
It begins with the fog. Tendrils of pale mist unfurl over the waves, disorienting the senses and shrinking the world to a grey shroud writhing with sorcerous life. 

Gradually, an impossible silhouette emerges, a towering prow, carved into the snarling visage of a vengeful god. Ramparts of ancient bedrock follow, bristling with elegant crenellations and buttresses inscribed with tormented elven runes. High above, soaring towers cluster against the night sky, vast, silent, and impossibly tall, their black spires crowned with witchfire, casting an eerie amethyst light about the structures. 

Fleetmaster Duriath Helbane plots to despoil human lands and conquer high elf outposts, hoping to win favour with Malerion, the Dread King. The _Temple of Spite_ is colossal, better considered a floating city rather than a ship. The ark is a setting where Characters can hide, infiltrate society, explore, and perhaps even destroy it from within. 

Along with a description of the ark and its denizens, you will find a broad overview of the dark elves’ tragic origins on Ulthuan, their homeland of frozen Naggaroth, rules for dark magic, and a host of creatures associated with Druchii civilisation. 

Few live to tell of such a sight. When the black ark comes, its cruel denizens follow, to raid, torment, and slaughter. From their inhospitable land of Naggaroth, the dark elves regard the world as a predator views its prey. They take what they want and relish in causing suffering. They feel no remorse, twisted as they are by resentment for a great historical betrayal. The Druchii hope to dominate all other species and destroy their high elf kin. 

_Temple of Spite_ provides a guide to dark elves abroad upon the world’s oceans. It positions the Druchii as unique antagonists for a GM to use in their campaign. Rather than sending Characters all the way to bleak Naggaroth, the book provides inspiration for bringing dark elves to them, wherever they may be hiding. 

The _Temple of Spite_ is a black ark, a floating citadel roaming the oceans, carrying a population of dark elves. Their society is a microcosm of Naggaroth, with the hierarchies, rivalries, intrigues, and cruelties of Druchii playing out in the towers and halls on board. 

Dark elves are as diverse as any intelligent species. A series of warbands and NPCs associated with the _Temple of Spite_ illustrate the many motivations and personalities across dark elf factions. None are restricted to the ark, so Characters might encounter them in the Old World, Norsca, Lustria, or elsewhere. All are worthy adversaries in a fight, though in the right circumstances, they can be patrons or allies. While dark elves revel in murder, torture, and cruelty, they are cunning enough to set aside sadism for long-term ambitions. The NPCs and guidance on creating dark elf characters help give them depth and nuance, to make them memorable and challenging villains. 

_Temple of Spite_ requires only the core **WFRP Core Rulebook** , but combining it with rules and background from **Sea of Claws** , **Sea Wardens of Cothique** , and **The Corsairs of Captain Flariel** will open up possibilities for new adversaries, expanded rules for bringing the dark elves to life, and provide a rich setting for an epic campaign.

## **Who Are the Dark Elves?**
_’We don’t fear the Druchii because they are evil, malicious, and sadistic, though they are. Nor because they are insane, for they are not. No, they terrify us because they_ are _us.’_ 

— Elthira Windshard, Lothern Merchant 

To Old Worlders, many of whom have rarely seen any sort of elf, the dark elves, or _Druchii_ as they are known in the elven tongue of Elthárin, are the stuff of nightmares, tales to scare misbehaving children. With skin of ice and teeth and nails of iron, they come during the hours of darkness to steal good people for their unholy feasts. Even in regions far from the sea, late night tales are told in taverns of elves riding daemonic horses who hunt humans for sport. 

To those with experience of elves, the truth is even more disturbing. The Druchii look like any other elves and, should they want to, blend in so well that they can move amongst Asur, Eonir, or Asrai undetected. Any elf one meets could be a dark elf, plotting in secret, waiting to strike. Their skin may be paler from life in bleak Naggaroth, their hair more commonly black, and they may prefer clothes whose designs call to mind death and blood, but they are still elves like their kin. They can be as courteous, intellectual, suave, and sophisticated as any diplomat from Ulthuan, and they can be monstrously, joyfully cruel. 

## **In Thrall to Dark Powers**
The dark elves deal with daemons and worship the _Cytharai_ , the dark gods of the elven underworld. Khaine, Lord of Murder, holds a special place in their culture. Academics might debate whether dark elves love murder because they worship Khaine or worship Khaine because they love murder, but to the Druchii, such an issue is just a meaningless distinction. 

It is not only humans hiding in their squalid towns and villages who fear ‘evil elves’. Quiet rumours in Marienburg say that the head of one Elftown clan was revealed to be a dark elf, though the Exarchate says nothing. To the rulers of the great port, that silence speaks volumes. The raiders who ravage Nordland’s coasts are not just Norscans, and reports have reached Elector Count Gausser that some among the Eonir have dealings with strange reavers in sleek black ships. For now, he holds his tongue, but should any hint of this reach the public, the demand for war with Laurelorn would be overwhelming, and it is a war he doubts he could win. 

## **In Their Own Eyes**
Ask a Druchii what they are and, while deciding how _precisely_ to maim you, they might deign to explain. The dark elves, like all other elves, are the children of Ulthuan, in this case the shattered kingdom of Nagarythe. In their worldview, they are the true followers of Aenarion and the devoted subjects of his son Malerion, the rightful heir to the Phoenix Throne. They were Ulthuan’s true warriors, the ones who held off Chaos, and the only ones who see the world as it really is: all the other peoples are cowards, imbeciles, or barely better than animals. They are superior and they alone are fit to rule. They are the Druchii. 

Human settlements are easy pickings for dark elf raids, and many a coastal village has been found empty of its population, grisly stains and smouldering ruins being all that is left behind. From time to time, sailors or coastal patrols find someone who escaped the elven corsairs, left wild-eyed and insane, ranting about the horrific fate of their fellows. Should any sensible folk living on the coasts of the Old World discover the full horror of the Druchii, they would flee far inland. 

## **History**
_’The history of these elves is one of blood and more blood.’_ — Sofia di Luccini, Tilean Scholar and Priestess of Verena 

The origins of the Druchii lie in the first war against Chaos, when the polar gates collapsed and daemons threatened to overrun the world. Ulthuan stood on the verge of destruction, until Aenarion rallied his people. They fought the daemonic legions to a standstill, but, even filled with the spirit of Asuryan, they could not push them back. Aenarion rejected the mage Caledor’s plan to drain the enemy’s magic from the world, and so the war remained a bloody stalemate. 

Hearing of the murder of his wife Astarielle, and the kidnapping of their children, an enraged Aenarion flew to the shrine of the murder god Khaine on the Blighted Isle. Inside the shrine he took up the Widowmaker, Khaine’s own fearsome blade, to wield against the invading daemons. 

Even imbued with the power of a god, Aenarion could not be in all places at once, and despite the valiant efforts of the elven forces the tide of daemons could not be stemmed. Chaos was only defeated with the sacrifice of Aenarion and Caledor and the formation of the Great Vortex, which syphons magical power to return it to the Realms of Chaos. 

But the damage to the elves was done, and the curse of Khaine’s touch corrupted Aenarion’s line. His second wife, Morathi, delved into blasphemous magics, while their son, Malerion, contemplated taking his father’s throne as his birthright. Rejected by the princes of Ulthuan in favour of an elected king, Malerion retreated to _Elthin Arvan,_ the Old World, to build an empire of his own. Years after his return, he crushed unrest in Nagarythe before trying to seize the Phoenix Throne in a treacherous coup. As his followers battled the assembled princes, Malerion dared the test of the flames of Asuryan, to prove his right to the Phoenix Throne, but he could not withstand the flames of the creator god and was horribly burned. 

The Dark elveS 

Morathi retreived her son, scarred by the flames and almost dead, and took him back to Nagarythe. From there, they launched a bloody civil war that almost conquered of Ulthuan, which came to be known as the Sundering. During this conflict, the Druchii were born. Morathi strived to unleash the daemons kept at bay by Caledor’s Great Vortex using sorcery, and Ulthuan’s mages wove counter-spells to thwart her, but the cataclysmic blowback of this arcane conflict shattered Nagarythe and much of Tiranoc. Malerion’s homeland was almost drowned beneath the angry seas. Dark elf sorcerers exhausted themselves to save what they could, and many of the fortresses and cities of Nagarythe became drifting citadels held afloat by their magic. 

Fleeing their defeat, the refugees sailed west, eventually coming to the bleak continent of Naggaroth where they settled to rebuild and plot revenge. Since then, Malerion has fixated on his driving desire for the conquest of Ulthuan and vengeance on those who denied him his birthright. His every command since the Sundering has that one goal at its root. For millennia, the black arks have sailed the globe, seizing captives, making dark sacrifices, and looting treasures across the world. 

Periodically, Malerion has attacked Ulthuan without success, his anger growing with each failure. Gathering the black arks, his armies invade in hope of at least seizing Khaine’s shrine and the Widowmaker his father once wielded. Each time, Ulthuan has held and defeated Malerion, but the Dread King lives on to plot and scheme anew. 

## **What Others Know of the Druchii**
The dark elves are not a secret in the Old World, but true knowledge of them and their goals remains elusive and, the farther from the sea one travels, the more fact becomes obscured by rumour, legend, and prejudice. 

The Druchii themselves contribute to this confusion. Physically almost identical to other elves, they can pass themselves off as their cousins when amongst lesser species, whether as mercenaries, traders, or simple travellers. It suits them to muddy the mental images others have of elves. 

The wood elves, of course, know the truth, but see no need to set others straight. The Asrai of Athel Loren have no contact with the sea and little in the way of relations with men. The Eonir of Laurelorn, faced with periodic threats from the Empire, have a complex relationship with the Druchii, as they too were wronged by the Asur. Yet they see no need to clarify the details of their history and dealings to humans, and their arrangements with the Druchii would be politically volatile if discovered. 

## **In the Old World**
Human Old Worlders hold varied opinions. The rulers of the great ports know enough to distinguish between elven subcultures. Even in taverns and ships’ holds, there are those who have survived a Druchii encounter who can swear they are far worse than the condescending elves of Ulthuan. 

Inland, the stories become more blurred. ‘Dark elves’ are only heard of as travellers’ tales, and the occasional atrocity or crime is attributed to elves in general. Some military leaders and scholars may possess insights into who and what the Druchii are, but they have more pressing concerns than educating the public on such matters. 

Dwarf opinions of the Druchii were forged by the ancient war between Karaz Ankor and Ulthuan. As far as dwarfs are concerned, the elves started it, the dwarfs finished it, and all this talk of ‘dark elf provocateurs’ is just a bunch of blame-shifting and excuse-making. Even direct testimony from seagoing dwarfs of Barak Varr about dark elf ships makes little difference; ‘elves’ is what it says regarding historical grievance in the _Great Book of Grudge_ s, and that’s all that matters to most dwarfs. 

When they raid Old World settlements, the Druchii strike by night and leave before help can arrive and they rarely leave witnesses. If they come to trade, they may pose as sea elves. When they offer their services as mercenaries or counsellors, they are vague about their origins, claiming to be from a conveniently distant elven realm. It is only in their dealings with the Eonir, Norscans, or corrupt folk in the Empire and Bretonnia that they openly present themselves as dark elves. 

## **Dark Elves in the Known World**
Dark elves almost never operate openly in the Old World, there is too much risk of their enemies there uniting against them. Elsewhere in the world, the Druchii are more brazen. Their black arks ply all the world’s oceans, launching ships to harry Asur holdings or raid for lost artefacts and captives to bring back to Naggaroth. 

Lustria is a favoured target for dark elf raids, not for captives, for the skinks and saurus who are native to the continent are far too obedient to their slann masters to make profitable plunder. Instead, swift black ships sail up Lustria’s many rivers seeking treasure and the complex magic of the Old Ones hidden in lost ruins and cities. Malerion, Morathi, and her sorceresses have an insatiable hunger for any powerful and exotic magic they might use to assail the elves of Ulthuan. 

For Characters starting out, tangling directly with dark elves would likely end in tragedy due to the intelligence and prowess of these foes. Try to keep an air of mystery and menace, a sense that something deadly is coming. Their influence should at first only be felt or glimpsed, perceived in the signs they leave behind, such as a type of weapon, the aftermath of magic, or the remains of a victim whose torturous end speaks to an unusual artistry. A handful of Druchii are best encountered at the climax of an adventure at this level of play. They make a substantial foe whose defeat can serve as the gateway to greater dangers. 

Farther south, dark elf ravenships are known to drop anchor at New Bechafen, seat of Luthor Harkon, ruler of the Vampire Coast. Perhaps it is for trade and resupply, though the frequent presence of the corsair Lokhir Fellheart at Harkon’s palace hints at an alliance against the Fortress of the Dawn, Ulthuan’s outpost at the continent’s southern cape. 

While the Druchii plague lands as far away as Ind, Khuresh, and Grand Cathay, for those who chart their reavings, their activities in the Southlands may cause the most concern. Rumours are shared in Lothern and Marienburg of a secret fortified port built somewhere on the continent’s western coast. What Malerion plans for this settlement is a troubling mystery. 

For more challenging games, dark elves come into their own as opponents. Characters might, for example, find themselves leading the desperate defence of a coastal village against a Druchii raid, though there should be more to the dark elves’ motivations than simple murder and pillaging. Naggaroth’s spies infest the coastal and riverine ports of the Old World and discovering and exposing their schemes could be a campaign in itself. The ease with which they can blend into polite society, even among other elves, and their willingness to be patient and manipulate others from deep cover make them subtle, yet deadly foes. In Lustria, Druchii raiding parties could be rivals for the recovery of lost artefacts or, as a twist, dubious allies in the face of an even greater threat. 

## **Dark Elves in Your Game**
Dark elves pose a challenge to even the most powerful Characters, whether as direct opposition in combat or scheming behind layers of deception. More than just blood-drenched villains, dark elves represent a civilisation that rejects everything Old Worlders hold dear. 

Like all elves, Druchii are generally physically and mentally superior to other species and should not be used as cannon fodder; they are not mere goblins to mow down like stalks of wheat. They are skilled warriors and their sorceresses are matched only by the slann and the mages of Ulthuan. Charming and erudite, blessed with silver tongues to match their powers of deception, dark elves are always looking for an advantage. Play them as calculating predators, continuously evaluating a situation for how it could improve their place in the Druchii hierarchy; or they can be ravening maniacs, but with a cunning and nuance that makes them all the more sinister. Even the possibility of an encounter with the dark elves should send a frisson of dread through Characters’ minds. 

For the most powerful or resourceful parties, struggles with dark elves can move from the Old World, or encounters in Lustria and elsewhere, to the realms of the Druchii themselves. Characters of a naval bent could lead ships to intercept dark elf raiders before they reach the Old World, capturing or sinking them in a desperate sea battle. Eventually, even the black arks, such as the _Temple of Spite_ , become a target. Perhaps the Characters’ mission is one of reconnaissance, rescue, assassination, aiding a faction in a mutiny, or even escape after capture.

## **The Continuing Kinstrife**
For games centred on elves, the Druchii represent a more personal threat, because they are kin. Indeed, for Asur Characters, they are an existential danger because Malerion wants them dead, or worse. Campaigns with high elves as a focus should keep in mind the long, bitter history of war between the two lands. Adventures might even entail trips to Naggaroth itself, infiltrating the cities and fortresses disguised as Druchii, trying to reach their goal before losing themselves to the siren call of Slaanesh and Khaine. For the Eonir, the question of how much they can deal with the Druchii before themselves surrendering to corruption becomes crucial, and wood elf Characters might be called upon to not only foil the Druchii in Nordland, but within Laurelorn itself.
